payload.title: [auth-saml-1] No signature-algorithm whitelist: weak RSA-SHA1 / SHA1-digest assertions are accepted
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-saml-1 (medium/crypto, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/saml.ts
LINES: 446-492

WHAT: createXmlCryptoSignatureVerifier() constructs `new SignedXml()` with no signatureAlgorithm/digest constraint and never inspects the SignatureMethod/DigestMethod that the document declares. xml-crypto 6.1.2 registers rsa-sha1 + sha1-digest in its default SignatureAlgorithms/HashAlgorithms maps (node_modules/.pnpm/xml-crypto@6.1.2/.../signed-xml.js lines 76-91), so an assertion signed with rsa-sha1/sha1 verifies and is accepted. Empirically confirmed: an assertion signed with `http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#rsa-sha1` + sha1 digest is accepted by runtime.verify(). The signing party (algorithm) is entirely document-controlled. (HMAC is NOT a concern here — xml-crypto leaves hmac-sha1 disabled by default and enableHMAC() is never called, so there is no HMAC/RSA key-confusion.)

IMPACT: SHA1 is collision-broken; accepting SHA1 XML-DSIG signatures lowers the cryptographic bar of the federation trust boundary and contradicts the module's 'no SHA1 if avoidable' intent. An IdP misconfigured to (or downgraded to) SHA1, or a future SHA1 chosen-prefix attack on the canonicalized SignedInfo, weakens assertion authenticity. Defense-in-depth/crypto-hygiene rather than an immediate full break.

SUGGESTED FIX: After loadSignature(), read the declared SignatureMethod/Algorithm and each Reference's DigestMethod and reject anything outside an allowlist (rsa-sha256/rsa-sha512, ecdsa-sha256/384/512; sha256/sha512 digests). xml-crypto exposes sig.signatureAlgorithm after loadSignature and ref.digestAlgorithm per reference — enforce the allowlist before trusting signedElementIds, and surface a SamlSignatureInvalid error for disallowed algorithms.
